title: Supply Chain Vehicle Routing Optimizer with Google OR-Tools, OpenStreetMap & FastAPI
problem: Last-mile delivery and supply chain logistics fleets waste thousands of fuel hours, fail strict delivery appointment windows, and incur excessive driver overtime costs when route dispatchers rely on manual scheduling or naive greedy distance heuristics. The Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) and capacity constraints is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization challenge where adding even 20 delivery stops creates factorial search spaces that overwhelm standard computing pipelines. This project builds a production-grade supply chain route optimization engine in Python using Google OR-Tools. The system models multi-vehicle capacity limits, customer delivery time windows, and driver shift constraints, calculates real-world distance matrices using OpenStreetMap, solves routes using Guided Local Search metaheuristics in under 15 seconds for 100 stops, and visualizes turn-by-turn routes on interactive React map dashboards.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Urban Last-Mile Parcel Delivery
use_cases.first_sentence: Urban courier delivery fleets dispatching 500 packages daily across 20 vans need optimal delivery sequencing to minimize total transit miles.
use_cases.second_sentence: The solver ingests delivery coordinates and parcel weight packages, generating turn-by-turn routes that reduce fleet vehicle mileage by over 22%.

use_cases.title: Grocery Cold-Chain Delivery with Strict Time Windows
use_cases.first_sentence: Fresh grocery delivery platforms promising 1-hour customer delivery windows must balance vehicle refrigeration capacities against customer arrival commitments.
use_cases.second_sentence: The OR-Tools routing model enforces strict time window boundaries, ensuring refrigerated delivery vans arrive within designated customer windows without perishable spoilage.

use_cases.title: Medical Specimen Hospital Pickup Fleet Dispatch
use_cases.first_sentence: Clinical diagnostic laboratories picking up laboratory specimens from regional clinics must guarantee sample pickup within 2 hours of collection.
use_cases.second_sentence: The optimization engine schedules on-demand hospital pickup dispatches, assigning couriers to priority clinic stops while respecting vehicle specimen volume caps.

hard_parts: Formulating the multi-vehicle routing problem (VRPTW) in Google OR-Tools with heterogeneous fleet capacities, drop-off service times, and penalty dropped-node costs
Configuring metaheuristic search strategies (Guided Local Search, Tabu Search) to escape local minima and converge to high-quality solutions within 15 seconds
Constructing and caching real-world distance and travel-time matrices using OpenStreetMap road network graphs without hitting external API rate limits
Handling dynamic route recalculations when emergency priority pickup orders are inserted into an active dispatch schedule mid-shift
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating the OR-Tools mathematical model, OpenStreetMap matrix calculators, FastAPI optimization routers, and React map views
Optimization benchmark proving >= 20% total route mileage reduction compared to nearest-neighbor greedy heuristics across 100 delivery stops

Anti-fake verification script adding an impossible constraint (stop demanding 500kg when max van capacity is 200kg) and asserting the solver drops the node with a penalty violation rather than crashing

architecture.data_flow: A dispatcher submits 100 delivery orders with customer coordinates, package weights, and delivery windows to FastAPI; the distance matrix worker checks its local SQLite cache for pairwise travel times (or computes Haversine/OSM routes) and returns a 100x100 matrix; the OR-Tools model creates the RoutingIndexManager, adds vehicle capacity constraints (max 1,000kg per van across 5 vans), and defines time window dimensions; the solver executes Guided Local Search with a 15-second time limit; the optimal route sequence, arrival times, and vehicle assignments return via JSON; the React dashboard renders delivery polylines and stop markers on an interactive map.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Hard constraint dimensions on vehicle capacities and time windows rejecting infeasible assignment combinations.

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU bound constraint programming algorithms and local web servers)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Python, OR-Tools, and open geospatial datasets)

riskiest_component.name: Combinatorial Explosion Causing Solver Timeout on Complex Time Windows
riskiest_component.mitigation: Set strict solver time limits (15 seconds) and use initial greedy heuristic solutions (PATH_CHEAPEST_ARC) before metaheuristic refinement.
riskiest_component.fallback: Cluster stops into geographical zones using K-Means and solve smaller sub-problems independently.
